title: Child's eye test with dilating drops (cycloplegia)
what: Your child gets eye drops that relax the eye muscle for a while. This lets the doctor find out exactly whether glasses are needed.
why: Before first glasses, if nearsightedness, farsightedness, or a squint is suspected, and to follow up on vision.
duration: drops and waiting usually take 30 to 60 minutes; sometimes drops are given at home for several days; results right away
tell_doctor: If your child has had an allergy to eye drops
If your child has heart disease, seizures, or other long-term illnesses

prepare.title: Plans
prepare.text: The drops can work from a few hours to a few days. Ask the clinic, and do not plan reading activities for that day.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Explain that the drops sting a little, but it goes away quickly.

prepare.title: Sun
prepare.text: Bring a cap or sunglasses. Light will feel too bright.

bring: Your child's glasses, if they have them
A toy or book for the wait
steps: A nurse puts drops in both eyes
Sometimes the drops are repeated several times
You wait for the pupils to get bigger
The doctor shines a special light into the eyes
The eyes are measured with a machine
The doctor looks at the back of the eye and explains the result
feel: The drops sting for a few seconds
Then light feels too bright, and it is hard to see up close
This is temporary and goes away on its own
after: While the drops work, it is hard for your child to read and draw
Protect the eyes from bright sun
If drops are prescribed at home, use them exactly as the doctor said
A glasses prescription is usually given right away
red_flags: A red face, fever, very dry mouth, or agitation after the drops: call the doctor
Your child is limp, very sleepy, or very restless: call emergency services

faq.q: Why use drops if you can just check with an eye chart?
faq.a: A child's eye works very hard and can hide farsightedness or show false nearsightedness. The drops relax the eye and give an accurate result.
With the right dose, it is a common and safe procedure. Tell the doctor about your child's health problems.

reminders.text: Eye test with drops tomorrow. Bring a cap or sunglasses for your child.
